purpose: Durable rotation registry for recovered and active long-form Warhammer 40K chronicles. Recovery backlog takes priority over new continuation work. Once recovered material is indexed and verified, rotate between distinct existing story lines rather than repeatedly extending one arc.

policy.chapterCapRule: Hard cap of 40 chapters per book. A continuing story that reaches Chapter XL must close that book at or before Chapter XL; further narrative continues as a subsequent book rather than Chapter XLI.

active.title: The Long Patrol of Broussard
active.sourceDocument: The Long Patrol of Broussard — Working Draft
active.recoveredThrough: X. THE FORWARD HOLDS — complete through Broussard organizing the search for Jerrik Noll, Edren Vale and Pallas Dorn and ending: “Let’s go find them.”
active.sourceObservedThrough: X. THE FORWARD HOLDS — complete; the connected Google working draft contains no later chapter.
active.currentEndpoint: XI. THE THIRD MAN — Broussard’s search team follows the smell of charred flesh and ozone into the forward hold service corridor and finds Jerrik Noll, Edren Vale and Pallas Dorn dead at an intermittently energized deck junction. Evidence shows Jerrik was electrocuted first, Edren died trying to help him, and Pallas became the third casualty when he tried to help Edren. Sella Varn identifies and helps isolate the emergency cross-feed; the bodies are recovered. Broussard accepts this as a genuine industrial accident while explicitly keeping the separate missing-telemetry mystery unresolved.
active.nextSlice: When Broussard next becomes rotation-eligible, continue after the bodies are recovered. The immediate missing-person problem is solved. Preserve that the electrocution was a real accident, not a disguised Genestealer attack. The next dependency-valid investigation can return to repair progress and the unresolved historical telemetry inconsistencies, but do not reveal the full falsified-origin/Genestealer truth before the narrative earns it. The book may contain no more than 40 chapters; if the narrative reaches Chapter XL, close the current book and continue any remaining arc in a subsequent book.
constraints: Fourteen-second telemetry gap is a surface anomaly, not the main plot hole.
Deep-indexed older telemetry was falsified to conceal the freighter's true port of origin.
Hesperant Vale crew is secretly compromised by Genestealer influence.
Genestealer hybrids are hidden among loose produce bins in the forward holds.
Broussard's detachment successfully returns the damaged freighter to the convoy after fighting additional High Presidio predators.
The reader sees the hidden Xenos travesty continuing beneath the apparent successful rescue.
Recover Google source sequentially and verbatim before fresh expansion.
Jerrik Noll, Edren Vale and Pallas Dorn died by accidental electrocution at an intermittent damaged service-junction cross-feed.
Jerrik was the first casualty; Edren and Pallas died in sequence while trying to help the man ahead of them.
The electrocution is a genuine mundane accident inside the larger mystery and must not be retroactively rewritten as a Genestealer kill.
Broussard still remembers the unexplained telemetry discrepancy after the bodies are recovered.
Hard cap: no book may exceed 40 chapters; Chapter XL is the latest permissible chapter number within a book.

active.title: House Vallimere’s Sons
active.currentEndpoint: Continuation II — The Practical Examination. The Three Admirals conduct a seventy-two-hour system-defense exercise that forces cadets—and themselves—to distinguish tactical victory from acceptable consequence. Prite adds Lesson Two to the replacement syllabus; Darcelle demonstrates confident maintenance-realism instruction; Renault explicitly recognizes that their old sacrificial simulation victories were play. Noble duel pressure remains active.
active.nextSlice: On the next House Vallimere rotation, continue from the developing replacement syllabus and the political consequences of the professors' practical doctrine. Preserve Prite's Lesson One and Lesson Two, Darcelle's growing confidence when anchored in technical instruction, Renault's calm humor under pressure, the Headmaster's protective institutional strategy, and Vane's Priority Omega protection. Do not reduce the arc to repeated duel jokes; political, doctrinal, and teaching consequences should advance.
